name: James Brown
hook: The bandleader who put the rhythm in charge of the song, and whose drummers' breaks became the most sampled sounds in hip-hop.
blurb: James Brown grew up poor in Augusta, Georgia, and became one of the most famous performers in the world. In the late 1960s he changed how his band played: instead of a tune on top, every instrument became part of the rhythm, and the first beat of each bar hit hardest. That was funk. His band is the biggest single source of sampled drums in hip-hop, which makes him this map's biggest sampled source under Q21. The breaks were played by his drummers, chiefly Clyde Stubblefield and John 'Jabo' Starks. On 'Funky Drummer' (1970) Stubblefield played a short solo, a break, that hip-hop producers later sampled more than a thousand times. Stubblefield made up his own patterns, and he never got credit or payment for their reuse, one of the plainest cases of how unequally the sampling business paid. Brown's own record includes a 1988 conviction after a police car chase, for which he served about two years, and arrests on domestic violence charges, including in 2004. He died on Christmas Day 2006.
